subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 56-year-old woman with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and coronary artery disease has an LDL cholesterol of 205 mg/dL despite atorvastatin 80 mg daily and ezetimibe. Evolocumab is added, and 4 weeks later her LDL cholesterol is 68 mg/dL. She has no new symptoms and her creatine kinase is normal.
question: Which of the following best explains the lipid-lowering action of evolocumab?

options.text: Binding PCSK9 and preventing degradation of LDL receptors
Activation of lipoprotein lipase through PPAR-alpha
Antisense inhibition of apolipoprotein B-100 synthesis

explanation_correct: PCSK9 binds the LDL receptor and directs it toward lysosomal degradation, reducing the number of receptors that return to the hepatocyte surface. Evolocumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds PCSK9 and prevents this degradation, so more LDL receptors remain available to clear LDL and plasma LDL falls dramatically on top of statin therapy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Irreversible inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase describes the mechanism of statins, not of an antibody directed against PCSK9.
explanation_incorrect.B: NPC1L1 blockade is the mechanism of ezetimibe, which this patient is already taking without adequate effect.
explanation_incorrect.D: PPAR-alpha activation with increased lipoprotein lipase activity is the mechanism of fibrates, which lower triglycerides more than LDL.
explanation_incorrect.E: Antisense inhibition of apolipoprotein B-100 describes mipomersen, a different lipid-lowering strategy that reduces VLDL secretion.

educationalObjective: Evolocumab lowers LDL by binding PCSK9 and preventing LDL receptor degradation, increasing hepatic LDL clearance.
